Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes January 15, 2025 The Centre at University Park Attendance: Ben France, James Ferstl, Samuel Ellis, Cannon Fletcher, Mike Bernardo, Summer Campbell, Quinten Whiteside Absent: Ron Bara, Chemia Woods, Quincy Grant, City Director-Capi Peck, City DirectorAndrea Lewis City Board of Director Liaison: City Director-BJ Wyrick LRPR/LRCAO Staff: Parks Director-Leland Couch, Deputy Director Administration Resources-Angela Nelson, Deputy Director Recreation-Shawanda Craig, Deputy City AttorneySimone Blagg, Courtney Perry-Safety and Training Coordinator, Administrative Assistant-Parks Director-Mahoganey Burkhalter, Kyndall Richardson-Secretary, Savanah Wells-Secretary Welcome: Chairman France welcomed everyone. Meeting called to order at 12:02 pm. Roll Call: Roll call completed. Seven (7) Commissioners out of Eleven (11) Commissioners in attendance. Quorum was established. Approval of Minutes Chairman France asked for a motion to approve November 2024 minutes & December 2024 minutes. Commissioner Campbell made a motion for the approval of the minutes. Motion 2nd by Commissioner Fletcher. Motion carried Citizen Communication: Ryne Pruitt w/ Walton Heights Staff Reports/Director’s Presentation/Events: Director’s Presentation: Director Couch presented on the following: • Budget Approval Review ❖ Commissioner Fletcher asked City Director Wyrick questions regarding the Budget review, Bond usage and ARPA funding. • Parks – Year in Review Highlights – 2024 by Marketing & Media Coordinator - Brittany Nichols. Presented by Parks Director -Leland Couch ❖ Request to send out Year End Presentation to the Parks Commission ❖ Commissioner Fletcher asked questions about Kiwanis Park opening. Presentation: • No Presentation. 1 Unfinished Business: • Subcommittee Reports ❖ Masterplan Subcommittee – Chair-JT Ferstl stated that they will have a standing meeting – the hour before each Commission Meeting. ❖ Marketing Subcommittee – Chair Quinten Whiteside Completed Exit Interview w/ Media & Marketing Coordinator Brittany Nichols and received a lot of great ideas and feedback to use going forward. ❖ Parks Conservancy Subcommittee – Chair Sam Ellis – advised that they’re working to get a meeting schedule setup. • Post Sales Tax Discussions – Agenda item has been covered and discussed previously. • Commission Ideas/Goals for 2025 ❖ Chairman France presented ideas for the Parks Commission to visit the Centers/Parks to learn more about these areas. Will bring a list of dates. Will work with City Atty to make sure that this is in line with the Bylaws. ❖ City Director Wyrick requested to see the Parks – Year in Review presentation at the BOD meeting ❖ Director Couch advised that the Parks Commission will need to present to the BOD according to the Bylaws. Discussed options for presentations for BOD and when to the present. Chairman France discussed with the City Atty and the commission the best way for this process. Commission discussed items to add to the Presentation. ❖ Request to schedule Parks Commission - BOD presentation. • Extending Parks Commission Meeting Time ❖ Discussed need to relocate meetings due to the facility closing ❖ Presented relocation options. ❖ Will table discussion and present written option next meeting. • Parks Newsletter – Brittany Nichols/Director Couch New Business: • Approved Budget Review. ❖ Agenda item was covered in Directors Report • Parks Director Item – New location for upcoming meetings. ❖ Agenda item has been discussed and tabled until the next meeting. Agenda items for next meeting: • Commission Ideas and Goals cont. • New Meeting location 2 • • • Center/Parks Visits Extending Meeting Time – Commissioner Smith Finalize details for Parks Commission - BOD Presentation Board – liaison Feedback • City Director – BJ Wyrick commend Parks and the Commission on the work that’s being done. Meeting Adjourned at 1:05 pm 3

Division Report: Operation Deputy Director: Justin Dorsey Parks Commission Meeting January 2025 • Highlights and Achievements o Urban Forestry: Planted 10 Willow oaks, 16 Zelkova’s and replaced a Chinese Pistache at the 2nd St grass lot. Replaced Maple in traffic circle at Allsopp Promenade. A large dead tree was removed at Westchester. Also removed a large dead tree at First Tee entrance. Removed large fencing pile at Reservoir Park. Removed old light poles on the ground at Kanis Baseball Field. Removed the old fencing at Reservoir Park. Removed several dead trees requested by Traffic Engineering. o Mowing Crew: Setup for grand opening at Kanis Park, cleaned park and new areas, detailed parking lots, cleaned bathrooms. Mulched leaves at Union, Remmel and several other parks. o Horticulture: Cleaned out and trimmed flower beds at Kanis Park, construction contractor had let them grow over. Continuing irrigation winterization. Reset Interstate field 5 for Central High Softball team practice. o Trail Crew: Repaired washed out areas on River mountain Trail system using mini ex and hand tools. Most of the damaged areas are now repaired. Repaired and cleaned up Backwoods Trail. o Downtown District: Landscape and tree trimming on Main Street corridor. Trimmed up trees, cut down stumps and refreshed beds. Purchased and put up the Christmas tree for City Hall Parks office. Removed furniture, installed a whiteboard and large screen in Parks offices. Cleared Cindy Island trails o Allsopp Restroom and Pavilion Roofs are being re-roofed in upcoming weeks. Certa Pro is painting the Chimney this week then the roofs will be done. o Centre on 12th – ITB is going out 1/2/24 and will go 21 days. o Dunbar Roofing – Board Approved. Ketcher has the contract and is being pushed to get this back to City Attorney office before the end of the week. o East Little Rock Construction – Classrooms are being worked on. Discovered the roof is leaking. Ketcher Roofing is working on a solution. I have also asked them to price the entire roof for us to consider. o Kiwanis trail paving – Awaiting a date to do the install of solar lighting. o MacArthur Pond repairs: Rented Trackhoe on site for digging of pond. The new Pump was installed yesterday, this is completed. o South Side Restroom Roof Completed. 1 Division Report: Operation Deputy Director: Justin Dorsey o Stephens HVAC unit is ordered. PO was done by Amanda Jones. 10 weeks lead time. Working with Lockeby to look at additional fencing to fortify this unit. o Stripping of Parking Lots in Progress after the first of the year: Big Dam Bridge, Boyle Park, Brodie Creek, and Otter Creek. o SWCC Renovation – NTP issued for 12.6.24. Painting and Gym floor Renovations are in progress. Renovations to the Banquet Hall will be after the first of the year. o Stephens Community Center – Work is progressing. Change order issued for extension to 2.2.24 due to Millwork being delayed. Some minor issues with the epoxy and a section of the Gym floor are being addressed. o Two Rivers Paving – 12.16.24 NTP for 12.17.24. Project will start 1.16.24 and will last approximately 2 weeks. We will need to announce the trail will be closed. o Wakefield Restroom – ITB is complete, It has been submitted for advertising o West Central – 12.17.24 Preconstruction complete. NTP will be for 1.6.24 to begin demo and first cuts of ball field. o Stephens Community Center – Work is progressing. Partition installed 12.4.24. The progress meeting moved to 12.11.24 at 11am. 2

Parks Commission Recreation - Report 1/15/2025 Senior Programs: Active and Aging The Aging & Active program returned from Thanksgiving break and started to prepare for their next Holiday Christmas. West Central held a bean Bag Baseball All-Star Game on December 5, along with polish sausage chili day. East Little Rock & Southwest celebrated the holiday on December 20. East Little Rock, Southwest & Stephens Community Centers These centers are under renovations and will be updated with flooring, lights and an overall brighter and appealing look. Therapeutic Recreation The month of December we had our Annual Therapeutic Recreation Christmas Program, it was held at Fellowship Bible Church in partnership with their Embrace Special Needs Ministry on December 19, we had a cast of 21 participants for this performance. Southwest Community Center Our cheerleaders continue to shine in the community, they participated in the Annual Southwest Christmas Parade on Saturday December 7, 2024. On December 5, 2024, we partnered with the Pulaski County Lawyer Association to provide a free service to those in need of clearing their records, over 250 participants attended. MacArthur Museum of Military History On-site visitation included 458 walk-in guests and 204 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. In addition to Arkansas, guests came from 20 states – as well as six foreign countries – Brazil, Canada, Ecuador, Germany, India, and South Korea. Outdoor Recreation Work has begun on mapping and layout for a new disc golf at Reservoir Park. Mapping of the old course layout and proposed layout provided by Crowell Engineering was done with Park's GPS/GIS specialist. The Cyclocross State Championships were held at War Memorial on 12/21/24. First–Tee Golf Although we experienced some slower periods this month, we have successfully maintained the golf course by clearing leaves and conducting tree trimming. Additionally, we promoted gift card sales for the upcoming holiday season. As we approach the end of the year, we are eagerly anticipating the 2025 golf season and the opportunities it will bring, including the introduction of new participants in this cherished sport. Youth Athletics Youth Basketball Season starts next month, registration is still going on at each location, the goal was to have at least 350 youth registered and to date there are 360. 1 Parks Commission – Recreation Report 1/15/2025 Dunbar Community Center After School Programs The after-school program at Dunbar Community Center wrapped up this month. Youth enjoyed our annual holiday meal on December 13th and received gifts from the center. Gifts included stuffed animals, games of their choice and Christmas pencils. We will start registration for the second semester on the 2nd of January online. Youth Basketball Program This month we continued practicing basketball our season start date is January 2025. All our teams added scrimmage games against each other to help prepare for the season. No practices were held during the LRSD Christmas break. Free Play During the last two weeks of the month the center was open to all youth to attend for free play in the gym. Staff was on hand to keep the youth safe and interacted with them in pick-up basketball. Special Event We hosted a Christmas paint party which was opened to anyone who wanted to attend. Participants chose from an assortment of designs the picture they wanted to paint. All pictures were relevant to Christmas. Fruit bags were gifted to all who came, and Christmas music played in the background. Stephens Community Center Star Student Afterschool Program: The Star Student Afterschool Program was a success for the first semester as we ended our participation with 48 kids signed up. The Afterschool Program had a great Christmas party on December 12, 2024. We gave the kids a snack bag with jellybeans in a Christmas ornament, apples, and oranges. They were also given pizza and a juice box. We also had them make their own Santa Clause where they had to color Santa and glue cotton on him to make his beard. Youth Sports Program Stephens had a total of (4) four teams for Basketball. We have 3–4-year-old, K-1st grade, 2-3 grade, and 4-5 grade. We also brought in a team; Olivia Chosen. We have been practicing at West Central and Dunbar Community Centers. Facility Vacancies: 2-Activity Assistants, and 2-Part-Time or 1 -Full Time Custodian Maintenance: Renovations for the building are going well. They have started putting the front desk together. The countertops to the bathroom and sinks have been placed but still in need of installment. The office has been painted and with new floors. In the kitchen area the upper and lower cabinets have been installed. West Central Community Center Youth Sports Program: West Central has approximately 180 participants for basketball season. Registration ends December 1st. We have 15 cheerleaders and have ordered new uniforms to begin their first season. Basketball practice has begun for all 20 West Central Teams. 2 Karate/Dance: The Karate and Dance programs have been on break most of December and will come back at the beginning of the year and will perform during halftime during the basketball season. West Central CC: We co-hosted Meet & Greet Toy Drive with Santa with the Black Fire Fighter Association. This event was held in the Gym and had a crowd of approximately 200 people. Little Rock Fire Department held their annual picture with Santa on December 21st for the Ward 6 Community. Rentals: The center had a total of 10 rentals for the month. Maintenance: All requests have been fulfilled. All flowerbeds have been mulched for the season. The construction on the baseball fields will start soon. Employment: We have a concessionaire, activity assistant and evening front desk receptionist to hire. Requisitions have gone out for these positions. Southwest Community Center Youth Programs: The afterschool Star Student Program enrollment numbers remain low, but we hope to see the increase once the afterschool transportation Pilot program has been approved. The Jr. Botanist program will restart in the spring with the focus educating our youth and teens on the importance of trees and plants. Jr. Botanist will meet every Thursday 6:00p.m. and Saturday 10:00a.m. Our weekly Art program is continuing to grow with a consistent 15-20 participants attending every Wednesday 6:00p.m. This month the group focused on creating holiday ornaments. Youth Athletics: We have a total of 7 basketball teams registered to participate in the youth basketball league which will begin January 6, 2025. Teams practice twice a week at 6pm at Dunbar Community until the renovation is complete at Southwest Community Center. Our cheerleaders continue to shine in the community, they participated in the Annual Southwest Christmas Parade on Saturday December 7, 2024. Adult Athletics: We are advertising and looking to host beginner’s pickle ball clinics and chair volleyball in the mornings. Dance workout is held every Tuesday and Thursday 6pm-7pm averaging 25 participants regularly. We now offer low impact senior workout via video in which the numbers have grown to 15 participants aging from 50+. Special Events: Every Wednesday night is community Art night. After the Art is completed, a display is placed in the lobby for guest and members to observe. The ACT prep classes will start up again in March collaborating with Pulaski County Youth Services, we look to serve at least 200 youth during this program. On December 5, 2024, we partnered with the Pulaski County Lawyer Association to provide a free service to those in need of clearing their records, over 250 participants attended. On November 28, 2024, ministries community church along with Southwest Community center hosted a soulful gathering from 11:00a.m.1:00p.m. 150 participates attended. Donation of clothing and food were received during the two hours. Renovations at the facility begin on December 6, 2024, focusing on remodeling the gymnasium, banquet hall and entrance area. The project is going well. ELR Community Center Starting to do work on the inside of the gymnasium. Work on the roof is complete. Painting the rooms on the breezeway, still installing lights in the gymnasium, 2 additional rooms were added, and work will continue until the projects are completed. The neighborhood meetings are still cancelled due to the ongoing renovation project and were moved the Community Park and First Baptist Church both located on East Ninth & Calhoun Street. Maintenance continues to mow, weed eat, and pick up around the entire grounds. Horticulture maintained the hedges and mulched flower islands. Continuing to assist with Active & Aging program and attend various meetings as scheduled. Little Rock Police Department continue to use the back area/field for their dog training, as needed. The community groups are still using the outdoor basketball/tennis courts and other areas to do exercises and fitness as weather permits. They are there 4 to 5 days per week, with about 8 – 10 people. There is still some of use of the field/park…daily/weekends, family 3 gatherings, tennis court (hopefully to be refurbished as multi-use courts) for walking and playing matches, and other activities. Senior Programs: Active and Aging The Aging & Active program returned from Thanksgiving break and started to prepare for their next Holiday Christmas. West Central held a bean Bag Baseball All-Star Game on December 5, along with polish sausage chili day. East Little Rock & Southwest celebrated the holiday on December 20. Baptist Health Monthly Screening and Outreach, Sage Health, and Oak Street Clinic continues to visit the various sites. Baptist Health continues their outreach at each center monthly. East Little Rock, Dunbar, Southwest, and West Central celebrated December Birthdays in various ways (from parties to shopping outings). They all also are continuing their outings, field trips, crafts, such as bottle flowers, jewelry, decorating caps/hats, puzzles, tshirts, and coloring. Dunbar Seniors: Coloring, String Jewelry, Bingo, Senior Circle, Walking, Connect Four, Dominoes and Line Dancing Class, Bean Bag Baseball, Chair Exercise Class, and Baptist Health Outreach Monthly Screenings, Go Fish, Painting, and FUNDAY. East Little Rock Seniors: Senior Fitness, Care Link workshop, Mind Bending, Silver Foxes Line Dance Class, Ceramics, Puzzles, Adult Coloring, Uno Card Game, Jewelry Making, Funtastic Friday, Nutrition Class and Funtastic Friday. Southwest Seniors: Bowling, movies, Skip-Bo, Pool Competition, Card Games, Bingo, Bible Study, Chair Exercise, Walking Club, Baptist Health Monthly Screening and Healthy Food Outreach, Arts & Crafts, Table Games, Ring Toss, Pool, Cooking Class, Funday Friday. West Central Seniors: Food Bank, Pickleball, Chair Volleyball and Bean Bag Baseball games vs. Various Centers (both teams), Bean Bag Baseball Practice (both teams), Bible Study, Birthday Shout Out. Therapeutic Recreation The month of December we had our Annual Therapeutic Recreation Christmas Program, it was held at Fellowship Bible Church in partnership with their Embrace Special Needs Ministry on December 19, we had a cast of 21 participants for this performance. We also had our last workday at the Little Rock Zoo. The TR Branch Out group decorated the tree and hung wreaths on the office doors at the Parks and Recreation at City Hall. This event took place on Dec. 5th. We will return to the zoo in March when the weather turns. The TR Branch Out program ended the Fall Session on December 20 with a Holiday PJ Party. Jim Dailey Fitness & Aquatics MEMBERSHIPS In December 2024, the facility sold a total of 1,729 monthly memberships, marking an increase from the 1,415 memberships sold in December 2023. FITNESS The 17 fitness classes at Jim Dailey Fitness and Aquatic Center are performing exceptionally well. AQUATICS The 6 aquatic classes at Jim Dailey Fitness and Aquatic Center are performing exceptionally well. SPECIAL ACTIVITY For the month of December, Baptist Health Community Outreach conducted a monthly blood pressure checks for our members and visitors, with a total of 12 individuals taking advantage of these services. The Centre at University Park The Centre has been on a joyride the month of December. We have enjoyed every meeting, party and much more. Catering to the needs of others is what we enjoy doing as a team. We started the month off with 100 active-duty police officers and cadets for an active shooter training. What a way to kick off the month! We then had the end of the year wrap up meeting with the directors and supervisor roles, it was great motivation for the upcoming year and how we will excel but also acknowledge the growth everyone has had in 2024. We’re also so pleased to welcome our regularly meetings such as: NUSA, Work order, Age friendly and the Parks Commission. Our facility is the hub for so many departments within the city and it gave us holiday joy 4 to see the Christmas events as well that we held here. The Housing Department hosting its annual Christmas gathering with 200 people to come eat, fellowship and enjoy each other’s company. That also led into the Parks Christmas gathering. Though the holidays are over the joy of the Centre never leaves. We’re so thankful for a month of greatness and new opportunities. Youth Athletics Youth Basketball Season starts next month, registration is still going on at each location, the goal was to have at least 350 youth registered and to date there are 360. They have done skills & drills and are now into their team practices. Games sites have been established due to ongoing facility renovations. Registration is still open for cheerleading. Kudos to all the staff at all centers for continuing to ensure everything is running smoothly. Adult Athletics Interstate/Allsop Park Program Field Rental reservations have ended for the year. LRSD Will have LR Central home softball games at Interstate. Adult Softball Program Interstate Adult softball registration for the spring league will begin January 15, 2025, for Men, women, coed and church league. Summer Playground Program We are working on making the summer playground program more enjoyable for the summer of 2025. First Tee Golf As we conclude this year, it is essential to reflect on our accomplishments. This year, we have successfully increased revenue at First Tee and welcomed numerous new and returning customers. A significant factor contributing to this success is the exceptional condition and quality of our golf course. It is paramount that we secure the necessary funding and resources to achieve our goals. While we occasionally encounter challenges in obtaining funding for specific projects within our organization, we must remember our primary objective: to provide recreational activities for the citizens of Little Rock and surrounding areas. Golf plays a vital role in enhancing the quality of life, offering a sport that families can enjoy together. With this in mind, we are in the process of developing various golf pass options for 2025, catering not only to individuals but also to families. Although we experienced some slower periods this month, we have successfully maintained the golf course by clearing leaves and conducting tree trimming. Additionally, we promoted gift card sales for the upcoming holiday season. As we approach the end of the year, we are eagerly anticipating the 2025 golf season and the opportunities it will bring, including the introduction of new participants in this cherished sport. Rebsamen Golf Reading course for the cold times coming up. We had over 40 ladies in attendance for our weekly lady’s day for the month of December slower than normal. Revenue for 2024 is still up 5% over 2023. Nike products has been approved to be ordered and will be stocked for 2025, in the pro shop. May have to cover greens sooner than normal, if the temperatures continue to fall and get to freezing. Looking to hire more staff in the beginning of the year. Rebsamen Tennis USTA singles leagues going very strong through December and into January. Monday night Rebsamen Singles league continuing through end of year (10-12 courts each week) and through the winter. Raul and Janan junior development groups going strong and are year-round (two week break for the holidays) Hired three new part time tennis aide positions, excited to have them on board. Working on filling out the 2025 tournament and league schedules. Being told that a large majority of USTA teams using public facilities are staying at Rebsamen or moving to Rebsamen due to the new court lights (great news!) 5 Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum attendance for December (through 12/30) was 2018. This number included: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visitation included 484walk-in guests and 204 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. In addition to Arkansas, guests came from 20 states – Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, New York, Nebraska, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah – as well as six foreign countries – Brazil, Canada, Ecuador, Germany, India, and South Korea. The museum's virtual documentaries/interviews received 469 new views during December for a total of 5,965views for 2024. Total attendance for 2024 is 43,415, which exceeds 2023 attendance by 0.5%. Museum staff continues to present off-site programming to children at Dunbar and Stephens Community Centers as part of the museum’s After School Program. During December, 199 children received instruction through this weekly outreach. Another 65 students were reached through the monthly 21st Century Program at J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy. During the fall semester, a total of 1,229 contacts were made with the After School Program as well as 192 contacts with the 21st Century Program. The museum raised $3,828 in December through donations bringing its total fundraising in 2024 to $35,000, exceeding its goal by 17%. Donations included $1,670 from the Aesthetic Club, $1,000 from the Carl H. Miller, Jr. Foundation, $500 from former Commissioner Paula Furlough and $300 from current Commissioner Pat Hoy. Gift shop sales for December were $695 for a total of $11,121 in 2024, which represents the gift shop's 3rd best year since the museum opened in 2001. The museum continues to host the traveling exhibit Two Minutes to Midnight and the Architecture of Armageddon. On loan from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, MO the exhibit will remain through January 5, 2025. After its de-installation, the museum will host another traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA. War Toys: Ukraine will open in early February and remain through August 11. The museum hosted AMR Architects on December 20 for a presentation on their winning design for the proposed MacArthur Unleashed shade structure. AMR presented a tentative budget for the project and discussed potential funding sources with the MacArthur Park Group and other interested parties. The museum and the Arkansas Koran War Veterans Memorial were included in an article about local tourism in the December 31 issue of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette. “Little Rock Offers Tours Covering All Sorts of Sights” by Jack Schnedler listed the various theme-oriented tours promoted by the Little Rock Convention and Visitors Bureau, including the “Little Rock Military History Tour” covering 14 locations. Special meetings and tours of the museum in December included: Seventy-seven members of the Aesthetic Club on December 10. Forty-five students and teachers from Bismarck Elementary School on December 18. Approximately forty family and friends for the holiday recital by students from the Margaret Wyatt Vocal and Piano Studio on December 22. Outdoor Recreation Work has begun on mapping and layout for a new disc golf at Reservoir Park. Mapping of the old course layout and proposed layout provided by Crowell Engineering was done with Park's GPS/GIS specialist. A meeting has been scheduled for the second week of January with the state PDGA's director (Professional Disc Golf Association) to discuss a proposal for an alternative course layout. A meeting with the director of ORCA (Orienteering of Central Arkansas) has been scheduled for early January to discuss layout and instillation of several orienteering courses in city parks. The final pop-up disc golf event of 2024 was held on 12/21/24 at War Memorial from 11am-3pm. Pop-up disc golf will resume in March 2025. The first event will take place on March 15th at MacArthur Park from 10am-4pm. I was the MC for the Ugly Sweeter 5k run on 12/21/24. This is the 3rd event I have MCed. I will be the MC for the 5k & 10k event on the weekend of the Little Rock Marathon. The Cyclocross State Championships were held at War Memorial on 12/21/24. I coordinated the event with the race promoters and oversaw the event on the day of. Weekly "Winter Wonders" (evening hikes at various parks) have been scheduled from 12/17/24 through late February. Work has begun on developing programming for Kanis Park. Programming will include basketball, skateboarding and birding activities. Preliminary work has begun on developing archery programming for the planned renovations of the range at Rebsamen Park. Work has been tentatively scheduled to begin in late Winter, '25. 6

Parks Commission Report January 2025 National Volunteer Week (NVW) – April 20, 2025 Impact the Rock: A Day of Unity and Service – April 26, 2025 Impact the Rock is the City’s annual Spring Day of Service. We offer 3 ways to participate. 1) Join one of our special curated beautification projects; we host a project in every ward. 2) We ask our adopters to work in their adopted area any time during NVW . 3) Residents can create their own project and submit their hours to the Volunteer Coordinator. Normally, we kick off NVW with Impact the Rock but NVW is on Easter this year. So, we are ending the week with it. Projects = TBA. Currently, we have 18 parks, 11 flowerbeds and 6 trails adopted. We also have 18 Volunteer Park Rangers.

This number included: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visits included 365 walk-in guests and 281 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. In addition to Arkansas, guests came from Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, Louisiana, Missouri, Montana, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas and Wisconsin, as well as from Canada, England, Germany, Japan and Switzerland. The museum's virtual documentaries/interviews received 619 new views during January. Museum staff presented off-site programming to 56 children at Dunbar Community Center and to 69 students at Stephens Community Center in January as part of the museum’s After School Program. Another 64 students were reached through the monthly 21st Century Program at J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy. The museum raised $2,155 in January through donations, including $1,000 from the Dale and Janice E. Davis Johnston Family Foundation. The museum has a goal of raising at least $30,000 each year in outside funding. The goal has been met each year since 2017. Gift shop sales for January were $199.56. Two Minutes to Midnight and the Architecture of Armageddon, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, MO was de-installed on January 9 and shipped to its next venue in Wyoming. The museum is preparing to host another traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA. War Toys: Ukraine will open on February 4 and remain through August 11. The exhibit draws attention to individual children and communities affected by war. Children often share their experiences and emotions through indirect methods of communication such as art and play. In the exhibit, internationally recognized photographer Brian McCarty collaborates with children who have been affected by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The museum has received a historical marker commemorating the contributions of African American soldiers in the Civil War. The cost of the marker was funded from a grant from the Arkansas Historical Marker Program as well as a private donor. Staff are working with Parks to schedule the installation of the marker behind the museum. A public unveiling of the signage has been scheduled for February 22. The museum hosted 78 members of the Aesthetic Club’s “Founder’s Day” celebration on January 28 commemorating the organization’s 142nd birthday. The women’s organization has been meeting at the Arsenal Building since 1984. Finalizing a contract for a leased golf cart for our maintenance crew. Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum attendance for February (through 2/26) was 1,611. This number included: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visits included 446 walk-in guests and 365 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. In addition to Arkansas, guests came from Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Iowa, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, 6 and Virginia as well as from France, Peru, South Korea and Spain. The museum's virtual documentaries/interviews received 574 new views during February. During February, museum staff presented weekly programming to 87 students at Dunbar Community Center and 63 students at Stephens Community Center as part of the After School Program. Another 76 students were reached through the monthly 21st Century Program at J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy. The museum raised $14,326 in February through donations and sponsorships, including $5,000 from Stephens Inc., $2,500 from the Legacy Capital Wealth Partners, and $1,000 from George and Linda Norton for the museum fundraiser in November. Former Commissioner Helen T. Leigh made her annual contribution of $4,500 to assist with maintenance of the museum lawn. In just the first two months of 2025 the museum has raised $16,481 towards its goal of raising $30,000 each year in outside funding. Gift shop sales for February were $573.14, which represented a 3% increase over February of last year. War Toys: Ukraine, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, opened on February 4, the exhibit was curated by Brian McCarty, an internationally recognized photographer who founded the nonprofit organization War Toys to address the effects of displacement and war-related trauma on children. The exhibit features photographs by McCarty in conjunction with artwork drawn by Ukrainian children in the summer of 2022 after the Russian invasion of their country a few months earlier. The exhibit will remain at the museum through August 11. The exhibit received coverage in the February 5 and February 10 issues of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette. More than 50 people attended the 2nd Annual Vintage Military Gear Show on February 16. The show featured original and reproduction memorabilia from Civil War, World Wars I and II, and Vietnam military from Arthur Eschenburg and Hayden Lang, two exhibitors from the museum’s vintage military vehicle show last October. A photograph of the event appeared in the February 17 issue of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette. In recognition of African American History Month, the Museum installed a historical marker commemorating the contributions of African American soldiers in the Civil War on February 22. The marker is located behind the museum in MacArthur Park. 55 people attended the dedication which included a program on the United States Colored Troops in Arkansas by Civil War historian Mark Christ. Among the guests were State Representative Denise Ennett and descendants of some of the soldiers who served in the USCT. News segments on the installation of the new historical marker appeared on both KARK Channel 11 and KLRT Fox 16. Links to the coverage are listed below. https://www.kark.com/video/historic-marker-unveiled-at-macarthur-military-museum-honoring-civilwar-soldiers-in-arkansas/10481267/ https://www.fox16.com/video/historic-marker-unveiled-at-macarthur-military-museum-honoring-civil-warsoldiers-in-arkansas/10481299/ Little Rock TV filmed the event, and a video is available via the link below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KjlYFmIvyY4 The “Movies at MacArthur” film for February was rescheduled due to inclement weather. The Search for Kennedy’s PT 109 was screened on February 26 and had 52 people in attendance. The March film, The Codebreaker, is scheduled for March 18 to commemorate Women’s History Month. The documentary relates the contributions of Elizebeth Smith Friedman, the ground-breaking cryptanalyst whose painstaking work to decode thousands of messages for the U.S. government would send infamous gangsters to prison in the 1930s and bring down a massive, near-invisible Nazi spy ring in WWII. Together with her husband, the legendary cryptologist William Friedman, Elizebeth helped develop the methods that led to the creation of the powerful new science of cryptology and laid the foundation for modern codebreaking today. The museum has finalized its 2025 schedule of “On the Road with Mark 7 Christ” bus tours of Arkansas Civil War sites. The next tour is scheduled for March 22 and will feature the Camden Expedition sites. The Camden Expedition was a Federal campaign that launched from the Arsenal grounds on March 23, 1864, returning to Little Rock on May 3. It was the final campaign conducted by the Union Army in south Arkansas during the Civil War and was designed to meet up with additional Union troops in north Louisiana and invade Texas. Stops will include battle sites at Prairie D ’Ane in Prescott, Poinson Spring, Marks’ Mills and Jenkins Ferry. Lunch will be provided at the McCollum-Chidester House in Camden, General Frederick Steele’s headquarters for the two weeks he was in that town. The fall bus tour, scheduled for September 6, will include Civil War sites in the Delta, including visits to Arkansas Post and Lakeport Plantation. Two members of the museum staff – Stephan McAteer and Shane Lind – successfully completed training in the Certified Tourism Ambassador program offered by the Little Rock Convention and Visitors Bureau. Trying to finalize a golf cart for the maintenance crew at Rebsamen. Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum attendance for March was 2,730. This number included: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) offsite programming and outreach. On-site visits included 906 walk-in guests and 955 visitors to special events, tours, etc. during the month. In addition to Arkansas, guests came from Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, and Wisconsin, as well as from Australia, Canada, Portugal and the United Kingdom. The museum's virtual documentaries/interviews received 517 new views during the month. Museum staff presented weekly programming to 58 students at Dunbar Community Center and 58 students at Stephens Community Center during March as part of the After School Program. Another 61 students were reached through the monthly 21st Century Program at J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy. The museum raised $5,263 in March through donations and sponsorships, including $2,500 from the law firm Wright Lindsey Jennings for the museum fundraiser in November. In the first quarter of 2025 the museum raised $21,744 towards its annual goal of $30,000. Gift shop sales for March were $1,380 for a total of $2,215 so far this year. War Toys: Ukraine, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, continues to receive favorable responses from visitors. The exhibit features photographs by Brian McCarty, an internationally recognized photographer, in conjunction with artwork drawn by Ukrainian children in the summer of 2022 following the Russian invasion of their country a few months earlier. It will remain at the museum through August 11. Museum staff is working with staff from the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts to develop partnership opportunities while the exhibit is in Little Rock. In celebration of March as Women's History Month, the museum featured The Codebreaker as its monthly "Movies at MacArthur" film. The documentary showcased the contributions of Elizebeth Smith Friedman, an American cryptanalyst who deciphered enemy codes in both World Wars and helped to solve international smuggling cases during Prohibition. Attendance at the March 18 screening was 74. For the first three months of 2025, attendance at the “Movies at MacArthur” program totaled 160 persons, representing a 68% increase over last year’s first quarter. Approximately 40 persons participated in a bus tour of Civil War sites associated with the Camden Expedition on March 22. The tour was led by Arkansas historian and author Mark Christ and included stops at Okolona, Prescott, Poison Spring, Camden, and Fordyce. The group enjoyed a catered meal at the historic McCollum-Chidester House in Camden. A summary of the tour was written by one of the attendees, Angie Faller, who also serves on the museum’s advisory board. In partnership with the 7 Civil War Round Table of Arkansas the museum hosted “An Evening with General Grant” on March 25 and “An Evening with President Grant” on March 26. Living Historian Dr. Curt Fields, who has portrayed General Grant in numerous films and who was selected as the official representative for the U.S. Grant Boyhood Home Association in Georgetown, Ohio, presented programs on Grant’s life as both Civil War general and President of the United States. Approximately 145 persons attended one or both nights of the program. A photo of Dr. Fields as General Grant appeared in the March 26 issue of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette. The museum will partner with the Clinton Presidential Library and Museum to celebrate Jazz Appreciation Month in April with music from the United States Air Force Band of MidAmerica. The Shades of Blue jazz ensemble will play a free concert at the Clinton Library starting at 6 pm on April 9th. The 18-piece jazz band offers something for everyone - classic and modern jazz literature; patriotic music; and some “pops” selections featuring their fantastic vocalist. The museum has begun a partnership with Freedom Sings Arkansas, a non-profit whose mission is to work with veterans and active-duty military to tell their stories through the process of songwriting. Local songwriters will meet with area veterans at the museum on the second Monday of each month starting on April 14. For more information on the organization, visit their website at: https://www.freedomsingsarkansas.org/ . Volunteer Division April 2025 National Volunteer Week (NVW) – April 20, 2025 #LRStrong: ReLEAF Rock Creek Trail – April 12, 2025 Impact the Rock: A Day of Unity and Service – April 26, 2025 Impact the Rock is the City’s annual Spring Day of Service. We offer 3 ways to participate. 1) Join one of our special curated beautification projects; we host a project in every ward. 2) We ask our adopters to work in their adopted area any time during NVW . 3) Residents can create their own project and submit their hours to the Volunteer Coordinator. Normally, we kick off NVW with Impact the Rock but NVW is on Easter this year. So, we are ending the week with it. All projects starts at 9 a.m. except for the Zoo’s projects. Parks Projects: Ward 2 - Benny Craig/Fourche Creek Ward 4 - Reservoir Park – Kick off; Planting trees; Lunch served Ward 5 – Rock Creek Trail #LRStrong: ReLEAF Rock Creek Trail is April 12th at 9 am. The non-profit KKAC has received a grant for 1000’s of trees, and we are planting 10,000 Oak saplings in RCT to replant what the 2023 tornado destroyed. Currently, we have 18 parks, 11 flowerbeds and 6 trails adopted. We also have 18 Volunteer Park Rangers. We have started a new volunteer recruitment campaign called “Be a Parks Hero.” Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be 1 checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

Therapeutic Recreation The TR Division will host the 23rd Annual Therapeutic Recreation Arts Festival on May 2, 2025, from 10:00am-1:00pm at the AR State Fairgrounds Hall of Industry. This annual event is in celebration of therapeutic recreation and provides a unique opportunity for the disability community to engage with children with special needs in Little Rock and across Central Arkansas by providing make it take it craft projects, games, hands-on experiences, etc. for children that attend this free event. Booths are provided by organizations, agencies, and businesses that either provide services for the disability community or have an interest in being a part of their community as a whole. The camp will run as follow: Monday-Friday June 9 -July 18 Time: 8:30 am-3:30 pm The Therapeutic Recreation Division uses education and recreation services to help people with disabilities develop and enhance their quality of life. This day camp is a therapeutic based program that emphasizes fun recreational activities for people with special needs to promote the development of motor skills, social skills, independence and other related areas. This camp is active, and days are filled with games, swimming, community outings, arts and crafts and more. Therapeutic Recreation The TR Division will host the 23rd Annual Therapeutic Recreation Arts Festival on May 2, 2025, from 10:00am-1:00pm at the AR State Fairgrounds Hall of Industry. This annual event is in celebration of therapeutic recreation and provides a unique opportunity for the disability community to engage with children with special needs in Little Rock and across Central Arkansas by providing make it take it craft projects, games, hands-on experiences, etc. for children that attend this free event. Booths are provided by organizations, agencies, and businesses that either provide services for the disability community or have an interest in being a part of their community as a whole. This is a great way for agencies to network and for teachers and families to learn more about services available for their children. The event will include 35 booths, a magician, a photo booth, arts and crafts, recreation activities and a dance contest! **TR Youth Summer Day Camp Registration opened on April 1st. The TR Summer Day Camp will be located at Fulbright Elementary School. Enrollment is full with 19 campers registered. We do allow for a waiting list. The camp will run as follow: Monday-Friday June 9 -July 18 Time: 8:30 am-3:30 pm The Therapeutic Recreation Division uses education and recreation services to help people with disabilities develop and enhance their quality of life. This day camp is a therapeutic based program that emphasizes fun recreational activities for people with special needs to promote the development of motor skills, social skills, independence and other related areas. This camp is active, and days are filled with games, swimming, community outings, arts and crafts and more. Each child completes an assessment process and receives an Individual Recreation Plan completed by the TR staff. This plan includes goals for each camper that staff will work on intensively throughout the camp process. Progress notes are completed daily to evaluate each camper’s progress. War Toys: Ukraine, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA and Mid-America Arts Alliance in Kansas City, has been extended through September 28. David Collins joined the museum staff as Museum Program Assistant on April 7. Mr. Collins has a Bachelor of Science in Education degree from UCA with a major in Secondary Social Studies. He has over six years of experience teaching in schools in Central Arkansas, most recently as the EAST facilitator at 8 Lonoke Public School District. He also has a Master of Arts in History from UCA and a Master of Arts in Public History from UALR. His museum/preservation experience includes serving as the Planning and Preservation Coordinator at the Capitol Zoning District Commission from 2019-2021 and the Public Programs Manager at Historic Cane Hill 2021-2023, where he developed and presented educational programming. The May "Movies at MacArthur" film, War Letters, is scheduled for May 20. The museum will offer two hours of PD credit to teachers who attend the movie and participate in a discussion forum with Museum Program Assistant David Collins. The museum hosted the final meeting of the Aesthetic Club's 2024-2025 season on April 22. Approximately 85 members attended. The organization will take a summer hiatus before resuming its meetings in October. The women's club has held its meetings at the Arsenal Building since 1894 and makes an annual contribution to the museum. The museum partnered with the Clinton Presidential Library and Museum to celebrate Jazz Appreciation Month on April 9 with music from the United States Air Force Band of Mid-America. The Shades of Blue jazz ensemble played a free concert at the Clinton Library to over 325 people. The museum hosted the first meeting of Freedom Sings Arkansas on April 14. The non-profit's mission is to work with veterans and active-duty military to tell their stories through the process of songwriting. Local songwriters will meet with area veterans at the museum on the second Monday of each month. For more information on the organization, visit their website at: https://www.freedomsingsarkansas.org/ . The museum hosted the Arkansas State Archives’ Spring symposium, Lost Utopias: The Search for Arkansas’s Vanished Tourist Attractions, on April 26. The event included presentations on Monte Ne, the history of Dogpatch USA, Hot Springs’ forgotten attractions, and the history of Arkansas tourism to its natural springs. The event was free to the public. To commemorate the 50th anniversary of the end of the Vietnam War, the museum hosted Lieutenant Colonel Ret. Hugh Mills Jr. for a program on April 29. A native of Hot Springs, Mills is one of the most decorated helicopter pilots in the Vietnam War and is the author of Low-Level Hell, A Scout Pilot in the Big Red One, which recounts his experiences in Vietnam. He discussed his experiences in the Vietnam War as well as his twenty-six year-career in the United States Army. Registration has opened for the 2025 MacArthur Park “History on the Run” 5k race on May 2. The race will begin and end in front of the museum and take runners and walkers through the MacArthur Park and Pettaway Park neighborhoods. Approximately 115 runners/walkers have already registered, including four corporate teams each from the UALR Bowen School of Law and L'Oreal. The museum will be a participating site in the Quapaw Quarter Association's 60th Spring Tour of Homes on May 10-11. This year's tour will focus on the MacArthur Park Historic District. The museum will appear in all publicity and promotional material for the tour. The museum will also, partner with the Clinton Presidential Library and Museum to open its America 250 celebrations on July 4, 2025, commemorating the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. The celebration will include free admission at the presidential center all day followed by a Revolutionary battle reenactment on the east lawn. The event is a presented in partnership with the Daughters of the American Revolution, the Early "Arkansaw" Reenactors Association, the MacArthur Museum of Arkansas Military History, and Blue Bell Creameries. Blue Bell Creameries will provide ice cream for the event. Special Tours at the Museum in April included: (1) senior group from Our Lady of Souls Church on April 10, (2) special needs elementary students from Stephens and Terry Elementary Schools on April 17, (3) 9 University of Central Arkansas's ROTC program on April 24, (4) two groups of 3rd grade students from Ridge Road Elementary in North Little Rock on April 25, and (5) students from Mountain Home Christian Academy on April 25. Volunteer Division June 2025 The Volunteer Coordinator attended the largest conference on volunteerism, Points of Light, from June 3rd – 6th. We have started a new volunteer recruitment campaign called “Be a Parks Hero.” Jr. Park Ranger Day Camp dates: June 9th-13th June 23rd – 27th July 7th – 11th Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects 1 We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

Volunteer Division July 2025 We have 16 new Jr. Park Rangers. The first week of camp had to be cancelled due to sickness but the other two weeks were a hot success. National Public Lands Day – Sept. 27th; Hindman Park; 9 am Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 1 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

This number included: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) offsite programming and outreach. On-site visits include 732walk-in guests and 159 visitors to special events, meetings, tours, etc. In addition to Arkansas, visitors have come from 31 states, including Alabama, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Louisiana, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, and Wyoming, as well as Australia, China, and Russia. The museum opened a new exhibition, Small Arms of the Civil War, in August. The exhibit features revolvers and bowie knives from the Bruce W. Brice, Jr. Collection which was donated to the museum in 2021. The museum is working on its exhibit schedule for the next two years. It has been approved to host a traveling exhibit from the National Museum of Civil War Medicine. From Darkness to Light: Photographs Along the Underground Railroad, a traveling exhibit from Exhibits USA, will be on display November 10, 2026, through January 7, 2027. The museum has also been approved to host Remembering the Forgotten War: Korea, 1950-1953 from the Naval History and Heritage Command in Washington DC from January 20, 2027, through October 20, 2027. Museum Program Assistant David Collins and Museum Intern Jessica Gates successfully completed the Little Rock Convention and Visitors Bureau's Certified Tourism Ambassador Training program in August. Volunteer Division September 2025 National Public Lands Day – Sept. 27th; Hindman Park; 9 am Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. 1 Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

Volunteer Division October 2025 Thank you to our chair, Ben France, along with the Mayor, Vice-Mayor and Dir. Joan Adcock for their support at Hindman Park on National Public Lands Day. Also a big thank you to our staff in Operations, Outdoor Recreation and Marketing who helped prepare for the day. Thank you to Starbucks too for donating coffee. We had about 35 volunteers. They painted the benches, bleachers and basketball goal posts. The baseball field fence is now clear of trees and other vegetation and can be repaired by staff. They also weedeated around the baseball field and the entire disc golf course. A lot of downed limbs were picked up and piled up at the curb along with trash bags. The volunteers were so proud and happy with their accomplishments and ecstatic when Taziki’s showed up. New friendships were forged; we strengthened community that day! Dir. Adcock said that the park hasn’t looked that good in years. Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 1 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

Volunteer Division November 2025 Compared to Quarter 1 – Quarter 3 in 2024, volunteerism in Parks and Recreation is up 6%. Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that park is not already under a contract. 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. 1 Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov. For Marathon, contact glamm@littlerock.gov. 2

Volunteer Division December 2025 The Commission’s interest in adopting a park is greatly appreciated. The recommended process is for the Commission to adopt a park and conduct an organized, monthly group cleanup or Commissioners can volunteer monthly at their leisure. For example, one commissioner might volunteer for 30 minutes one day while another one volunteers for 30 minutes another day. Adopt-a-Park Requirements 1) Volunteer at least 2 hours a month either as an organized event or individually at your leisure. 2) Parks provides tools such as weed eaters, loppers, shovels, and rakes. We also provide litter grabbers and trash bags. 3) Volunteers receive a free pavilion rental per calendar year. 4) Volunteers receive a sign with their name on it. 5) Hours are turned in by the end of each month. Park Adoption Recommendations 1) Kanis Park 2) War Memorial Park Volunteer Opportunities 1) Volunteer Park Ranger (VPR) VPR’s are ambassadors, stewards and protectors of our park system. They officially represent the city, beautify our parks and are extended eyes and ears for the LRPD and Parks. Uniforms and training are free and VPR’s are expected to volunteer for 16 hrs./month. 2) Adopt-A-Park, Trail or Flowerbed We have over 50 open spaced parks, over 20 miles of soft surface trails and ~30 flowerbeds. Adopters spend at least 2 hrs./month in their adopted area. Tools can be checked out and trash bags, flowers, mulch and soil are free. Adopters receive a sign with their name/org. on it and one free pavilion rental per calendar year. 3) Park or Trail Clean-up An org/individual/family can schedule a clean-up by contacting Karen at ksykes@littlerock.gov. We ask that all vols schedule with us to ensure that the park is not already under a contract. 1 4) Jim Daily Aquatic and Fitness Center We need volunteer fitness instructors to expand our programming. 5) Rebsamen and First Tee Golf Courses Vols marshal, clean golf carts, pick up balls, etc. 6) Community Centers Vols are needed to coach various sports programs and help with special events. 7) Eagle Scout Projects We have various projects that Eagle Scouts can work towards. 8) Marathon Vols are needed to help with their races throughout the year. 9) #LRParksPushyPlants Parks has committed to removing 10%/year of our invasive species. We need help mapping them using iNaturalist and removing them/cutting them back. Sign up at www.littlerock.gov/volunteer. Any volunteer opportunity working with a vulnerable population (children, senior citizens, etc.) must pass a background check. Parks pays for it. Questions? To volunteer at a brick and mortar, contact that facility directly. To volunteer for the adoption programs, #LRParksPushyPlants, Eagle Scouts, clean-ups or VPR, contact ksykes@littlerock.gov.
